effect: Debug mode: Z + Start in a stage opens [BOMBERMAN ACTION MENU], and L on the pause screen opens the in-game debug menu
note: The master debug flag. The game clears it at start-up and nothing in any of the three ROMs can set it: a write trap from power-on through the title, file select, a stage, Game Over and Continue saw no write (US ROM), and seven button sets held at power-on did nothing. Held from the first frame, the boot, title and file select come up normally and the menu opens with buttons only. Run on the US and European ROMs. Tested as a held RAM write in BizHawk, not on a GameShark.

effect: Debug mode: Z + Start in a stage opens [BOMBERMAN ACTION MENU], and L on the pause screen opens the in-game debug menu
note: The debug flag on the Japanese ROM, whose menu carries the build tag DBG---1998/03/15-A where the others say MASTER ----- DEBUG. Tested as a held RAM write in BizHawk, not on a GameShark.

effect: 4 bombs, fire 3, 50 gems, and health fixed at 2 bars
note: Four bytes of the player block: extra bombs (0-3, the HUD shows one more), extra fire (0-3), gems, health. Maximum health is 80165245. Picture: before, and with all four held. The fire byte scales the blast (0.60, 0.90, 1.20, 1.50 for 0-3); with the bomb byte at 3 two tapped bombs were out at once, which never happened at 0. Holding B throws up to four at once with or without the code. Tested as a held RAM write in BizHawk, not on a GameShark.

effect: 4 bombs, fire 3, 50 gems, and health fixed at 2 bars
note: The same four bytes on the Japanese ROM, six lower. Tested as a held RAM write in BizHawk, not on a GameShark.

effect: 7 lives
note: The pause screen shows 07. Tested as a held RAM write in BizHawk, not on a GameShark.

effect: 7 lives
note: Lives on the Japanese ROM. Tested as a held RAM write in BizHawk, not on a GameShark.

effect: No damage
note: The debug menu's NO DAMAGE switch, which the damage routine tests on its own (80023CB8), so it works with the debug flag off. Picture: the penalty for falling out of the map, health 4 to 3 without the code and 4 with it. On the US ROM it also held against enemy contact and two bosses, the contact forced by writing Bomberman's position onto them. Tested as a held RAM write in BizHawk, not on a GameShark.

effect: No damage
note: NO DAMAGE on the Japanese ROM, same test. Tested as a held RAM write in BizHawk, not on a GameShark.

effect: Hold Z to fly: A rises, B sinks, the stick moves; Z + L ends the map
note: The debug menu's G BUTTON DEBUG switch, which works with the debug flag off. Flying was run on all three ROMs; Z + L, which jumps to the Clear Points tally and loads the next map, on the US ROM with the flag on. Tested as a held RAM write in BizHawk, not on a GameShark.

code: Debug flag on: hold Z + Start in a stage
effect: [BOMBERMAN ACTION MENU]: GAME START, MAP NUMBER, MAP TEST, CAMERA TYPE, TITLE TEST, ENTRY EDIT, MUSIC NUMBER, SOUND NUMBER, DEMO, SHOCK TEST
note: With the debug flag on (GameShark 8016E424 0001; Japan 8016E41B 0001). The game's main thread runs this menu whenever the game loop returns, and only Z + Start with the flag on makes it return. The Control Stick moves the cursor and changes values, A selects. TITLE TEST is an empty case, and MAP TEST loads a map without one of its data files: HUD on black.

effect: Loads any of the game's 192 maps, 00-BF
note: With the debug flag on (GameShark 8016E424 0001; Japan 8016E41B 0001). 00-7F are playable maps and 80-BF cutscene and event maps. All 192 were loaded on the US ROM. Picture: map B3.

effect: Restarts the game with a ready-made save in the fourth file slot
note: With the debug flag on (GameShark 8016E424 0001; Japan 8016E41B 0001). 1-4 start Planets 2-5; 5 is Planet 5 Garaden at map 7 of 7; 6 is Planet 6 Gossick with every stage at 5 and all 24 collectibles; 7 is Garaden with 23 of 24. 0 is a normal boot. All eight run on the US ROM, 1 and 6 on the other two. Picture: the file select after GAME START 6, and its boss stage.

effect: Plays the cutscenes: 1 is the fireworks ending scene, 2-5 introduce the Bomber Jet, Marine, Copter and Slider
note: With the debug flag on (GameShark 8016E424 0001; Japan 8016E41B 0001). 0 and 6-9 all play the control-room opening. The scenes were not watched to the end.

code: Action menu: MUSIC NUMBER, SOUND NUMBER
effect: A sound test taking 0-100 hex for each
note: With the debug flag on (GameShark 8016E424 0001; Japan 8016E41B 0001). A plays the number; music 5 and 23 and sound 101 were checked by recording the output, not by ear. The game's own Sound Test in Options lists BGM 00-31 and SE 001-127 by name.

effect: A Rumble Pak test: TOTAL TIME, ON TIME, OFF TIME
note: With the debug flag on (GameShark 8016E424 0001; Japan 8016E41B 0001). Opened on the US ROM; the rumble itself was not checked.

effect: An object-placement editor running on the chosen map
note: With the debug flag on (GameShark 8016E424 0001; Japan 8016E41B 0001). SET MODE shows the object number, its NAME_ label, position, angle and three parameters; L cycles SET, RESET and SAVE MODE. SAVE MODE sends the list to a print routine that is empty in the released game, so it does nothing. Opened on the US ROM; the controls are from the code.

code: Debug flag on: pause, then L
effect: [MAIN MENU]: TIMER BAR, DEBUG DISPLAY MODE, NO DAMAGE, NO ATTRIBUTE, G BUTTON DEBUG, BOM, FIRE, DISPTYPE
note: With the debug flag on (GameShark 8016E424 0001; Japan 8016E41B 0001). L again goes to [LIGHT EDIT] and [FOG EDIT]; Start closes it. Opened on all three ROMs; the lines were changed on the US ROM. The lines have their own cards below.

effect: [LIGHT EDIT] and [FOG EDIT]: live editors for the map's lighting and fog
note: With the debug flag on (GameShark 8016E424 0001; Japan 8016E41B 0001). Ambient and diffuse colour and light direction; fog colour, range and far plane.

code: In-game debug menu: DEBUG DISPLAY MODE
effect: 1 prints Bomberman's position and the map's STAGE, AREA, MAP and CLEAR numbers; 2 prints player and camera positions
note: With the debug flag on (GameShark 8016E424 0001; Japan 8016E41B 0001). Picture: mode 1 with the timer bar, and mode 2.

effect: Floor types stop working: an exit floor no longer ends the stage
note: With the debug flag on (GameShark 8016E424 0001; Japan 8016E41B 0001). 8016E404 (Japan 8016E406). The floor-type handlers return at once while it is set; damage floors go through another routine (80086AD0) and still hurt. Shown on map 0A's exit floor: the stage ends on the Clear Points tally without it and carries on with it (picture). With it a current floor stops carrying Bomberman (map 19) and a lift column stops lifting him (map 45). Spikes (map 10) and a hot plate (map 58) took a bar of health with it on as with it off. No floor type changes friction: the snow maps slide like any other floor.

effect: Changes what is drawn in the distance on some maps
note: With the debug flag on (GameShark 8016E424 0001; Japan 8016E41B 0001). 80177974, which each map sets for itself. On map 2B the far road is missing at 0 and 1 and drawn at 3 and 5 (picture: 0 and 3); four other maps showed no change. What each value means is not settled.

effect: A frame-time bar with three counters along the bottom of the screen
note: With the debug flag on (GameShark 8016E424 0001; Japan 8016E41B 0001).

effect: Sets the camera number, 0-10
note: With the debug flag on (GameShark 8016E424 0001; Japan 8016E41B 0001). The same variable each map sets for itself. Held on map 02: 2 is the map's own view, 4 a close view from the far side, 6 a higher side view (picture: 4 and 6) and 7 a low view from outside; 0, 1, 8, 9 and 10 showed only sky.

code: Score 5 on every stage of Planets 1-5 with all 24 collectibles
effect: Planet 6, Gossick, appears on the planet select and on the Score screen
note: At a stage clear the game sets a save flag when all 24 collectible bits (the nn/24 counter on the pause screen) are held and every stage of the first five planets has a score of 5. The planet select then shows six planets once Garaden is cleared. On the US ROM the game set and saved the flag itself when the last missing stage was finished with a score of 5, played a short scene of the planets with no text, and drew Gossick after a power cycle; the finish and the score were forced, not played. Its third stage is listed as Vs.???? even once cleared. Picture: the same file without and with the flag. GameFAQs lists it as all the Other-Dimension bombs and five Gold Medals.

code: Score 5 on every stage of three, five and six planets
effect: Options gains Slider Race, then Golden Bomber, then Millian's Treasure Hunt
note: The Options screen counts the planets whose every stage has a score of 5: three open Slider Race, five Golden Bomber, all six Millian's Treasure Hunt. Shown on the US ROM by setting the scores on a save file: two planets give neither (picture, left), three and four give Slider Race, five add Golden Bomber and six add the Treasure Hunt. The planet result screen calls such a planet Bomber Hero · Gold and gives it a gold medal. Any five do for Golden Bomber: Gossick is only the sixth planet in the count, and three gold planets plus a gold Gossick do not give it. The Japanese ROM opens the Treasure Hunt on another rule: Gossick's three stages cleared at any rank, even with only four gold planets. GameFAQs gives Slider Race for 3 Gold Medals and the Treasure Hunt for 6, as here, but Golden Bomber for clearing Gossick's three stages; Golden Bomber did not appear with Gossick gold and only three other gold planets.

effect: A timed one-on-one Bomber Slider race against a rival
note: Started from Options on a file with everything unlocked. The result scene reads your time back, then the race starts again; nothing was written to the save file after two wins, and the game's text has no best-time line. The wins were forced with the debug finish, not raced.

effect: A gold Bomberman plays three scored stages of his own
note: Maps 6F, 70 and 65, after an intro in the control room. Nothing was written to the save file. Its ending scenes were seen only by loading their maps.

effect: The planets are replayed to find 24 treasures
note: "Scattered about the crash are 24 treasures. Please find them!" The pause screen gains three 0/8 counters.

effect: A celebration scene at Millian's castle plays once, then the game returns to Options
note: "We have prepared a celebration for you!" When the set becomes complete during a Treasure Hunt stage the game plays map B0; nothing is unlocked and no flag is set. Shown on the US ROM by setting the 24 treasure bits of the save file in a stage and forcing the finish: the scene followed with nothing more written. The treasures were not collected by play. Picture: the pause screen at 8/8 three times, and the scene.

code: Press Start 12 times, quickly, on the first screen after switching on
effect: The file select gains a seventh entry, Bonus: a White Bomb mission of three stages
note: The first screen is the HUDSON logo in Japan and the licence screen in Europe. The game counts Start presses there: 10 to 14 inside one second, with no pause of 7 frames or more, set a flag until the power goes off (read from the controller code, 8001DCEC). The file select then shows Bonus under Stereo (Japan: おまけ). Played on all three ROMs with the pad alone, one press every 5 frames: the entry appeared, also on a blank save, and A on it started the mission: "Good work, White Bomb! Here's the next mission", the Bomber Jet leaving, then stages on maps 2B, 49 and 54 and a Total Score. The three stages were ended with the debug finish, not played, and nothing is saved. Picture: Bonus selected on the US ROM, and the briefing. GameFAQs lists tapping Start rapidly while the intro plays; during the movie it did nothing, on the first screen it works.

code: Sound Test: hold C-Left or C-Right, then C-Down
effect: The band on the Sound Test stage turns, and C-Down turns it back to the front
note: Options, Sound Test. About half a degree a frame. C-Down is read only while neither C-Left nor C-Right is held, and sets all four players back to facing front. Played with the controller. Picture: turned with C-Left, and C-Down.

effect: A developer test of the Controller Pak and the cartridge's save memory that nothing in the game calls
note: Routines 80020550 and 80020844, with no caller or pointer anywhere. Run by pointing the scene callbacks at them (8016526C and 80165274). It shows each controller port's pak status, a pak note list on L, and four actions. EEPROM DATA WRITE overwrites the first 200 hex bytes of the save memory with a test pattern, erasing all four files, and EEPROM DATA READ reads it back; both were run. The two PAK lines need a Controller Pak and were not.

effect: Fourteen checkerboard test rooms: most empty, 7B with rows of treasure objects, 7C and 7E with enemies and pickups laid out
note: Nothing points to them: not the stage-select table, any map's exit list or any map number in the code. Loaded with MAP NUMBER. 7B's list is 24 balls and eight each of three other treasure objects. 7D is different: Bomberman on the Bomber Copter in Planet 3's red canyon. Picture: 71, 7B, 7C and 7E.

effect: A blue-brick room with a red curtain wall, four times over, and a starfield with no floor
note: Unreferenced in the same way. BC-BF sit in the cutscene range and have no HUD.

effect: One small unused room beside each group of stages, in that group's tileset
note: Maps 01, 07, 14, 1A, 20, 24, 2C, 34, 3A, 3F, 48, 4B, 56, 5B and 60, all with a blank stage record and nothing pointing to them. Picture: 01, 2C, 4B and 60.

effect: An alternate first room for Planet 3's first stage, and a Bomber Copter scene in the same canyon
note: Both carry the stage record 3-1-1, but the stage select starts that stage on map 98 and then 27. 26's only exit leads to 27.

effect: 17 of the game's 652 objects are placed by no map and created by no code; one is a blue X crate
note: 304 objects are in no map's placement list (US ROM 2193A0): 30 blank slots and 274 named. The US ROM's code creates 257 of the named ones; that was read from the code and the callers were not traced. The 17 left are seven spare item slots (ITMDUMMY9-15), SOFTBLK3, CRASH2, CRASH3, GAGON_F, NGOGL_IC, ENDL_TG, BAL_WD, MEG_FB, BAG2_BR and MCH_00. Picture: SOFTBLK3 put into test map 7B's list by hand. Placed the same way, the dummy items and MCH_00 hang the map load and the rest show nothing.

effect: A design chart headed "Bomber Base" in Japanese and English, left in the corner of the font texture
note: US and European font texture (US ROM 64C3C0); the Japanese ROM's font is a kana sheet without it. Whether the game ever draws that corner was not determined.

effect: 652 developer names for the game's objects, shown only by the object editor
note: Fixed-width strings such as NAME_ITMBOM, NAME_FLASH1, NAME_EVCRAFT_B1 and NAME_MAPWOOD2 (US ROM 1172F8). Also left in: "sbrk : can not change data segment space allocation!" and the editor's output lines.
